findings.finding: The sell-side bar for FY27 underlying PBT (£13.0m at all three brokers cited) sits at the low end of an unchanged £12-15m company guide that management reaffirmed at the AGM with trading 'in line', so a straight reiteration at the interims clears the bar rather than meeting it at the top.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide reiterated at FY26 results (23 Jun 2026): -0.18%; at AGM update (29 Jul 2026): +2.72%; Dec 2025 interims with unchanged expectations: -2.01%. Guidance cuts: Nov 2024 interims -36.24%, Mar 2025 trading update -45.70%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock has sat at 37-40p since August on exactly this information. If the market expected a raise, the stock would have run into the print (20d run-up +1.06%, 5d -2.94%); it has not, so reiteration is roughly the priced case and only the low-end placement of the bar is a mild cushion.

findings.finding: Order momentum disclosed since FY26 results: UK&Europe order book £534m at 1 Jul (from £507m), £375m due in 12 months (vs £324m at 1 Nov 2025), data-centre wins in UK/Germany/Sweden, JSSL book £327m, plus a place on Network Rail's £70m steel-piles framework (14 Oct 2026, starts Jan 2027) supports H2 volume.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these figures are four months old and the framework is a non-RNS website item worth little near-term. What is unpriced is the 1 Nov order book figure the release will carry, which nothing sourced predicts.

findings.finding: FY27 delivery depends on larger, higher-margin projects starting later in the year after several already slipped into the back end of FY27, while UK construction activity weakened in October (PMI 43.6 from 46.1, commercial 46.3, sentiment lowest since May); this company has twice turned H2-weighted guidance into a warning (Nov 2024 interims -36%, Mar 2025 -46%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance cuts: 2024-11-26 interims -36.24%, 2025-03-03 trading update -45.70%; FY27 guide introduction (31 Mar 2026, cautious) +3.35%.
findings.why_not_priced: The slippage is known and was built into the cautious guide; the October PMI deterioration is macro and not transmitted by the company or a direct counterparty, so this is a tail risk, not a sourced miss. If the market were pricing a cut the stock would have de-rated into the print and the short register would be building; it is flat and covering (0.38% to 0.29%).
findings.independence: UK construction PMI October 2026: https://www.itv.com/news/2026-11-05/construction-activity-falls-on-slump-in-housebuilding-amid-severe-headwinds ; peer Billington (H1 to June 2026) calls the structural steel market 'challenging' with competitive pricing: https://www.directorstalkinterviews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/BILN-Interim-Results-Sept-2026-RNS-Final.pdf

findings.finding: H1 net debt is likely to print above the £28.2m year-end: £20.7m of bridge remedial provisions remained at March with 'the majority of the associated cash outflows' expected in FY27, alongside Modular Solutions closure cash, against an H1 profit the company says is low-margin; management targets only broadly flat net debt for the full year, helped by a c.£10m contract advance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dec 2025 interims headlined net debt down to £21.7m (helped by £20m insurance proceeds) and the stock fell 2.01% anyway; FY26 net debt cut to £28.2m on results day: -0.18%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference from disclosed provisions, not a disclosed H1 figure. Analysts will have modelled some outflow, but the H1 headline net debt figure has not been given anywhere and a rise against last year's falling H1 figure is the kind of line that can be sold on a day the guide is merely reiterated.
findings.independence: Edison FY26 note: net debt targeted broadly flat despite c.£20m non-underlying cash outflows, £10m contract advance received after year end: https://www.edisongroup.com/research/fy26-in-line-strategic-reset-targets-higher-returns/BM-3578/

findings.finding: A person closely associated with NED Cynthia Gordon bought 39,814 shares at 38p (£15k) in the market on 7 Oct 2026, the only discretionary insider purchase since the AGM (the CEO's buys are an automatic monthly £726 salary plan).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction to PDMR dealings on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Small, public and from a non-executive, so weak evidence; it is a buy shortly after the H1 period end, before the closed period, which a director would be unlikely to make knowing of a guidance cut.
findings.independence: Perpetual increased its holding to 12.05% on 13 Oct 2026: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/severfield--sfr/holding-s-in-company/9823440

findings.finding: Closest listed UK peer Billington Holdings reported H1 2026 (to June) revenue +29.1% to £53.95m and PBT +70.1% to £2.84m on a record order book, implying structural steel volumes recovered over a period overlapping Severfield's H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction of SFR to peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer proxy and public since September; Billington is a fraction of Severfield's size and serves different sectors, and its own statement calls pricing competitive, which is Severfield's stated margin problem. Weak transmission.

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': order-book finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1 (July AGM data), guide-reiteration finding from +0.6 to +0.4 (lands inside the guide)
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (Luceco): H1 net-debt finding raised from -0.4 to -0.5
'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': H2-delivery tail finding cut from -1.0 to -0.8, and p_up moved from 51 to 49 on the net of the two changes
'Size the move on what is new; reaction history moves p_up not abs_move': abs_move_pct kept at 5.5 (new H1 numbers, thin turnover) rather than cut toward the 3.07 median
